methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $9M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Infinite Machine is a Seed-stage transportation company founded by Joseph Cohen and Eddie Cohen. The company has raised $9.3M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises six private Transportation companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and EarthGrid; no public transportation comparables were identified as sufficiently analogous.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a $23M median valuation. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $9.3M total raised as a proxy for current valuation, reflecting typical Seed-to-next-stage expansion. The resulting implied valuation is $23.25M. A peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Transportation sector; while six private peers exist in the broader sector, none qualify for narrow-filter comparison (fewer than three datapoints at matching stage or valuation tier). Drawing on all-sector peers would introduce material distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $20M (low) to $27M (high), with a median of $23M. This range reflects the single applicable triangulation method and carries meaningful uncertainty inherent to Seed-stage assessment. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer benchmarks at this stage and early revenue/traction visibility typical of the stage. The range should be refined as additional comparable financing rounds or operational milestones become available.
